summary: This paper from the Journal of Policy and Development Studies (2023) examines how tax evasion and avoidance affect economic development at the grassroots level in Nigeria, using a descriptive research method. It reviews literature on tax revenue, personal income tax evasion, tax avoidance, MSME compliance, and causes of evasion, and draws on Tax Morale Theory and Institutional Theory. Its findings are that evasion reduces government revenue, worsens inequality and weakens governance, while avoidance can stimulate investment but erodes revenue when excessive. It recommends stronger tax enforcement, fair policies, taxpayer education and international cooperation. The text provided is truncated before the full recommendations section.
one_line: A 2023 Nigerian study on how tax evasion and avoidance undermine grassroots economic development and what policy responses are needed.
key_facts: The study 'Effect of Tax Evasion and Avoidance on Economic Development of Grassroots in Nigeria' was authored by Asomba Ifeyinwa U, Owa John T and Chime Jessie Onyinye of the Department of Public Administration, Enugu State University of Science and Technology.
The paper was published in the Journal of Policy and Development Studies (JPDS), Vol. 14, Issue 2 (2023).
The article was received on 2nd November 2023 and accepted on 27th November 2023.
The study adopted a descriptive research method technique.
The study found that tax evasion reduces government revenue, exacerbates income inequality, and undermines governance.
The study found that tax avoidance can stimulate investments but can erode government revenue when practiced excessively.

Ofoegbu et al. (2016) found a positive and significant relationship between tax revenue and economic development in Nigeria, emphasizing tax policies based on the human development index rather than solely GDP.
Chukwugeku & Mmamefune (2022) revealed that personal tax evasion has a significant negative implication for socio-economic development.

The MSME tax compliance study found that tax penalty and tax fairness have positive and significant influences on sustainable economic growth, while perceived opportunities for tax evasion have a negative and insignificant influence.

The paper identifies high rates of taxation, complexity in tax laws, shortage of experienced personnel, moral and psychological factors, and attitude of the income-tax department as causes of evasion and avoidance.
Toby (2003) is cited as observing that tax evasion erodes moral values and builds up inflationary pressures.
The paper cites Appah (2010) for the claim that a large part of government income is collected through tax revenue, so evasion and avoidance severely affect development.
Erich Kirchler, an Austrian psychologist, is presented as a proponent of Tax Morale Theory, which links tax compliance to attitudes about fairness and legitimacy of the tax system.
The paper's keywords are Tax, Tax avoidance, Tax evasion, Economic growth and development, and Nigeria.
The DOI given for the article is 10.4314/jpds.v14i2.2.
